title: Linux Boot: From Power On to Services

scenes.say: When you power on a Linux server, what really happens before your app runs? Let's break down the boot process.

scenes.label: Firmware
scenes.sub: BIOS or UEFI checks hardware, then runs GRUB.
scenes.say: First, firmware like BIOS or UEFI checks your hardware, then launches the bootloader—usually GRUB.

scenes.label: Kernel
scenes.sub: GRUB loads the Linux kernel and initramfs.
scenes.say: GRUB loads the Linux kernel and a temporary root filesystem called initramfs.

scenes.label: systemd
scenes.say: The kernel starts up, then launches systemd as process ID one. Systemd is the parent of everything else.
Systemd brings up the default target, like multi-user or graphical, then starts and supervises all your services from unit files.

scenes.question: What does systemd replace?
scenes.right: It replaces init and manages all services.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: systemd doesn't just replace the old init script. It manages all services and their dependencies.
